data.title: Why Is Penny Stock SunCar Technology Group (SDA) Up 132% Today?
data.description:
SunCar Technology Group (SDA) stock rocketed higher on Friday after the Chinese automotive company announced preliminary earnings and a share repurchase program. Starting with earnings, the company revealed unaudited revenue for the first nine months ending September 30, 2026 of approximately $426.4 million. This would mark a 25% increase when compared to its revenue from the same period of 2025.

SunCar Technology Group noted that its revenue growth was largely due to improvements across its various sectors. For example, unaudited Auto Services Revenue is expected to increase 22% year-over-year to $185.4 million. The company also expects its Auto eInsurance revenue to reach $197.4 million, which would be a 32% year-over-year increase. It also noted that Technology Services revenue for the period should increase 19% to $43.6 million.

"Looking ahead, the company will continue to capitalize on China's large automotive services market, its continuous path to full digitalization, and the rapidly expanding EV segment, actively pursuing new potential partners and capturing key new verticals," said SunCar Technology Group CFO Eric Zhang.

SDA Share Repurchase Plan

SunCar Technology Group also announced a share repurchase plan today. Its Board of Directors has approved the repurchase of $10 million worth of SDA stock. The company said that it will fund these purchases with cash on hand and cash from operations. These repurchases are set to take place from time to time over the next three months.

Investors reacting well to a share repurchase makes sense. They often improve investor morale and signal confidence from the company's leadership team.

SDA Stock Movement Today

SDA stock experienced a strong 131.92% rally on Friday. However, the shares were still down 92.43% year-to-date and have fallen 92.15% over the past 12 months.

With today's preliminary earnings and share repurchase news came heavy trading of SDA stock. This saw some 443 million shares change hands, compared to a three-month average daily trading volume of about 552,000 shares.

Is SunCar Technology Group Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for SunCar Technology Group is Moderate Buy, based on one Buy rating over the past three months. BTIG analyst Marvin Fong reiterated this rating on September 25, 2026. He also lowered his price target for the shares to $4 from $5, suggesting a possible 2,514.38% upside for the shares. data.title: AST SpaceMobile Stock (ASTS) Set for 19% Move After Q3 Earnings Next Week, Say Options Traders
data.description:
Space satellite firm AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) reports its Q3 earnings next week – November 9. The company's share price is down 58% in the year-to-date, hit by increased competition from rival SpaceX (SPCX) and its plans for expansion and space data centers. However, it climbed higher today on news that it is building a heavy-lift rocket to take its satellites to space.

As such, Wall Street has a Moderate Buy consensus on the stock. Meanwhile, the options market is pricing in a big 19% move, either up or down, after it releases the Q3 earnings report.

What the Options Market Expects for ASTS Stock

According to TipRanks' Options tool, the options market is expecting a big move of 19% in either direction after the results.

ASTS has a recent history of sharp post-earnings moves, although the reactions have varied from quarter to quarter. After its last earnings report on August 10, 2026, the stock climbed 4.17% the day after publication. The day after its May 11, 2026, report it fell 11.62% and after its March 2, 2026 report it grew 6.63%.

The expected 19% move then either up or down post the Q3 earnings next week would be a significant movement. That shows that this is an important set of results for ASTS investors.

The ASTS stock has traded between $28.98 and $133.86 over the past year and has a beta of 1.48, meaning it tends to move more than the broader market.

What Wall Street Expects

Wall Street analysts expect AST SpaceMobile to report earnings per share of minus $0.42, compared with minus $0.45 in the same period last year. Revenues are tipped to come in at $45.73 million compared with $14.7 million this time last year. The previous quarter's sales results were $31.52 million.

Will ASTS beat Wall Street forecasts? As can be seen below, it has a pretty weak track record of beating expectations in recent quarters.

data.title: Anthropic's Valuation Could Be Cut in Half to $1 Trillion After Market Rout
data.description:
Multiple media reports say that bankers are now eyeing a potential valuation for artificial intelligence (AI) startup Anthropic of between $1 trillion and $1.3 trillion following the market meltdown on Nov. 5. A valuation of $1 trillion would be half the $2 trillion that the company was seeking a month ago as it announced plans to hold its initial public offering (IPO) by the end of November this year.

The media reports say that bankers looking to take Anthropic public are considering the reduced valuation as the AI trade falters and U.S. markets experience extreme volatility. The technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index on which Anthropic will trade under the ticker symbol "ANT" fell 5.5% amid a marker rout on Nov. 5. Since Oct. 1, the Nasdaq has declined 10% and entered a correction.

Anthropic's estimated valuation. Source: TipRanks

Anthropic's Growth

Reports or a lower valuation also come after Anthropic released a revised S-1 investor prospectus on Nov. 2 that showed slowing growth at the company in this year's third quarter. Concerns of slowing growth are likely to also impact of Anthropic's valuation as the company looks to raise more than $100 billion from its upcoming IPO.

Additionally, there are worries about what the Democratic victory in the midterm elections means for the AI infrastructure buildout going forward. The left-leaning Democratic Party now takes control of the U.S. House of Representatives and Senate. Many Democratic lawmakers have called for a moratorium or outright ban on the construction of AI data centers and other infrastructure.

Will Anthropic Go Public?

While bankers focus on the valuation of Anthropic, there are growing doubts that the company will even go public this year. Odds that Anthropic holds its IPO before Dec. 1 of this year have plummeted on prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi, dropping from 80% before the midterm elections to about 50% today.

The midterm election results are seen as a repudiation of the AI movement and data center construction across America, with voters registering their anxieties about the technology and the threats it poses to jobs and the environment. Anthropic's main rival, OpenAI, canceled its plans to hold an IPO this year, citing market conditions.

data.title: Dow Jones Midday Report: DJIA Muted Despite Upbeat Jobs Report and Improving Consumer Sentiment
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is down 0.07% on Friday as investors assess a labor market and consumer sentiment update. The Bureau of Labor Statistics announced this morning that nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000 in October, topping expectations of 70,000. The professional and business services sector added the most jobs at 70,000, followed by healthcare with 42,000.

Furthermore, August's job gains were revised up to 186,000 from 133,000, while September's increased to 60,000 from 29,000. The U.S. economy has now averaged 86,000 job gains per month this year, up from 10,000 in 2025. Meanwhile, the unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%, below the estimate of 4.2%. The rate has remained between 4.1% and 4.3% since March.

A higher-than-expected consumer sentiment reading from the University of Michigan is also supporting the Dow Jones. The preliminary Index of Consumer Sentiment reading for November came in at 51.0, up from 48.0 in October and above the estimate of 48.0. In addition, consumers now expect year-ahead inflation of 4.3%, down from 4.7%. Long-term inflation expectations fell to 3.4% from 3.5%.

Which Stocks are Moving the Dow Jones?

Let's pivot to TipRanks' Dow Jones Heatmap, which illustrates the stocks that have contributed to the index's price action.

Nvidia (NVDA) is leading the tech sector higher after Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said she doesn't oppose data centers, but rather opposes companies building facilities without consulting local residents or addressing their concerns. Hinojosa's comments helped drive a recovery in AI stocks.

Elsewhere, most sectors in the index are mixed, including financial, communication services, and consumer defensive. Both Alphabet (GOOGL) and Amazon (AMZN) are in the green, while Chevron (CVX) is trading higher as well despite falling oil prices.

Is the Dow Jones a Good Long-Term Investment?

The SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) is an exchange-traded fund designed to track the movement of the Dow Jones. As a result, DIA is falling alongside the Dow Jones today.

Wall Street believes that DIA stock has room to rise. During the past three months, analysts have issued an average DIA price target of $601.12, implying upside of 16.76% from current prices. The 30 holdings in DIA carry 28 buy ratings, two hold ratings, and zero sell ratings.

data.title: Fox Closes $22 Billion Deal to Buy Roku to Expand Streaming Reach past 100 Million Homes
data.description:
Fox (FOX) finished its $22 billion purchase of Roku (ROKU) on Friday, creating a television giant that pairs live broadcast networks with a leading connected TV platform. Fox Class A shares rose 1.83% to $66.43 on Friday, while Roku shares closed at $160.30.

First announced in June, the deal gives Fox direct access to more than 100 million households that use Roku devices and smart TVs. Combining Fox's live sports and news with Roku's software will help the cable-reliant broadcaster grow its online audience and better target digital ads.

"The closing of this acquisition advances the long-term strategy of FOX," Fox Chief Executive Officer Lachlan Murdoch said in a statement. "Beginning today, our top priority for the combined company is to continue to relentlessly serve audiences and partners, while reinforcing the openness and choice that is the essence of the Roku platform."

Fox Pays Cash and Stock while Targeting $400 Million in Cost Savings

Under the merger terms, Roku investors receive $95.30 in cash and 0.9799 shares of Fox Class A common stock for each Roku Class A and Class B share they owned before closing, according to a company filing. Following the buyout, former Roku stockholders own roughly 26% of Fox's outstanding shares, while existing Fox investors keep the remaining 74%.

Fox expects the tie-up to deliver about $400 million in annual cost savings within two years of closing. Management also projects that the deal will add to free cash flow per share by the second full year. Allen & Company LLC and Morgan Stanley (MS) acted as financial advisors to Fox, while Qatalyst Partners advised Roku.

Anthony Wood Joins Fox Board to Co-Chair Digital Unit

Roku founder Anthony Wood is joining Fox's board of directors and will serve as co-chair of a new division called Fox Digital Platforms. Wood will lead the unit alongside Paul Cheesbrough, who becomes co-chair and CEO of the division.

Fox Digital Platforms brings together Roku, the free ad-supported Tubi streaming service, the Fox One streaming platform, and podcast producer Red Seat Ventures. Fox launched Fox One and bought Red Seat Ventures in 2025 as part of an ongoing push beyond traditional cable television.

"We started Roku more than two decades ago to give people a better way to watch TV, and that mission doesn't change today," Wood said in a statement. "FOX has a deep respect for Roku's culture and wholly shares our commitment to staying open to every content partner."

Is FOX a Good Stock to Buy?

Turning to the Street, FOX stock carries a Moderate Buy consensus based on two Buys and one Hold rating assigned in the past three months. The average 12-month FOX stock price target is $90, which implies 52% upside from the current price. (See FOX stock forecast)

data.title: Tesla (TSLA) Merger with SpaceX Thrown Into Doubt After Midterm Elections, Says Dan Ives
data.description:
Closely followed technology analyst Dan Ives says that a potential merger of Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) has been thrown into doubt following the U.S. midterm congressional elections. Ives says that Democrats who now control both the U.S. House of Representatives and Senate are likely to make any merger between Elon Musk's two publicly traded companies difficult.

"We will believe a SpaceX/Tesla merger ​happens but ⁠now faces a much tougher regulatory roadmap to get this deal done in 2027 given this new political blue roadmap in DC/Texas," said Ives, who is a partner and senior managing director ⁠at Yorkville ​Ives & Co. Musk said on SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call in October that a merger with Tesla would be a "good idea" and that special committees at the two ​companies were exploring a potential deal.

Tesla's key performance indicators. Source: TipRanks

The Midterm Results

Doubts about a Tesla-SpaceX merger are growing after Republican lawmakers suffered a resounding defeat in the midterms. With most ballots counted, the Democrats hold 54 seats in the U.S. Senate versus 44 seats for the Republican Party. In the House of Representatives, the Democrats are on track to win more than 250 seats, there best showing since 2008.

The Democrats will now be able to put a check on the policies of Republican President Donald Trump, who's tariffs and war in Iran have proved deeply unpopular with the electorate. They are also expected to be less pro-business and could also kibosh corporate mergers and put a moratorium on the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure buildout, both of which would impact Musk's businesses.

Tesla Cancels the Cybertruck

Ives comments on the SpaceX merger come on the same day that Tesla announced it is ending production of its Cybertruck. Musk announced on social media that the company will end Cybertruck production at its Texas manufacturing facility by the middle of 2027. The Cybertruck is being discontinued so that Tesla can make room for increased production of its self-driving Cybercab.

Tesla sold fewer than 100,000 Cybertrucks in the U.S. through September of this year, and sales in 2025 declined 48% year-over-year to 20,237 vehicles. The futuristic looking Cybertruck proved polarizing with consumers, with people either loving or hating the vehicle's appearance. The Cybertruck was unveiled in 2019. Tesla initially projected that it would sell 250,000 Cybertrucks a year, but actual sales were much lower than that figure.

Is TSLA Stock a Buy?

Tesla stock has a consensus Moderate Buy rating among 27 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on 14 Buy, 11 Hold, and two Sell recommendations issued in the last three months. The average TSLA price target of $402.47 implies 4% upside from current levels.

data.title: Why Is the Stock Market Up Today, 11/6/26?
data.description:
Both the S&P 500 (SPX) and the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) are trading higher on Friday with gains of 0.92% and 1.88%, respectively. The gains come after both indexes plunged on Thursday, suffering their steepest single-day declines since the April 2025 tariff crash.

Earlier this week, Gina Hinojosa beat Greg Abbott to become Texas' first Democratic governor since 1995. That sparked concerns of a slowdown in AI growth, as the Democrats have called for stricter regulations on AI and data center development. In addition, Texas accounts for nearly 30% of planned U.S. data center capacity. However, Hinojosa told CNN that she won't ban new data centers in Texas.

AI Stocks Recover as Labor Market Shows Strength

Instead, she wants to ensure that data center companies listen to local residents and address their concerns before building new facilities. "It is not that I hate data centers," she said. "I hate the way they are taking advantage of Texas and that stops when I'm governor." Hinojosa's comments helped drive a rebound in AI stocks, including Nvidia (NVDA), AMD (AMD), and Intel (INTC).

Elsewhere, an upbeat jobs report has also lifted sentiment. In October, nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000, well above the 70,000 estimate. August's job gains were also revised up to 186,000 from 133,000, while September's were revised up to 60,000 from 29,000.

data.title: Dan Ives Calls Tech Rout a "Golden Buying Opportunity"
data.description:
Wall Street analyst Dan Ives said that Thursday's 5.5% plunge in the Nasdaq Composite created a "golden buying opportunity" in AI stocks after Democrats swept the November 3 midterm elections. The index suffered its worst day since April 2025 and entered correction territory, down nearly 12% from its October 6 record.

Ives compared the selloff with the market drops during the COVID-19 outbreak in March 2020 and the tariff shock in April 2025. He believes that investors are pricing in an end to the U.S. AI infrastructure expansion, even though he expects construction to continue at a slower pace.

For context, Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa wants to temporarily stop new projects until stricter rules are introduced. UBS analysts estimate that restrictions like these could affect about 30% of the new U.S. data center capacity planned for 2028.

However, this does not mean that those projects have been canceled. Instead, some could face construction delays or have trouble getting the approvals they need.

Why Ives Still Expects Heavy AI Spending

Ives now expects growth in AI infrastructure spending to peak in 2027 instead of 2028 or 2029. Even with that earlier peak, he forecasts $3 trillion to $4 trillion of AI-related investment over the next several years. He also believes that major technology companies will spend more than $1 trillion on AI in 2027 alone.

Recent company results help explain his forecast. E-commerce and cloud giant Amazon (AMZN) expects approximately $220 billion in total cash capital spending this year, although that includes investments outside of AI. Software giant Microsoft (MSFT) reported $45.2 billion in capital expenditures in its latest quarter, while revenue from its Azure cloud business grew by 48%.

However, Microsoft also reported delays in receiving computing capacity from outside suppliers. That shows why strong demand alone cannot guarantee that construction will stay on schedule.

Ives argues that projects with permits already in place should keep moving forward, and expects most facilities planned for the next 18 months to be built.

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100. This is based on 89 Buys, 12 Holds, and zero Sells assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. Furthermore, the average QQQ price target of $983.96 per share implies 49.6% upside potential. (See QQQ Stock Forecast).

data.title: S&P 500 Rebounds After Worst Selloff Since April 2025 as AI Stocks Rally
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SPX) is up 0.97% on Friday following a brutal trading session the previous day that saw the benchmark index plunge 4.4%, its worst day since the April 2025 tariff crash. Fears of slowing data center development from a Democrat-controlled Congress contributed to the decline, although comments from Texas' governor-elect have helped ease those concerns.

Gina Hinojosa, who beat Greg Abbott to become Texas' first Democrat governor since 1995, said she doesn't hate data centers. Instead, she believes that some companies who build data centers have taken advantage of Texans by building them in their communities without properly listening to residents or considering how these projects affect them. Nearly 30% of planned U.S. data center capacity is located in Texas.

"It is not that I hate data centers," she told CNN. "I hate the way they are taking advantage of Texas and that stops when I'm governor."

AI Rebound, Jobs Report Drive S&P 500 Higher

Hinojosa added that a strong AI industry in Texas and protections for its people are not mutually exclusive. Furthermore, communities should have a say in where data centers are built and how these projects affect their neighborhoods, she said. Her comments helped drive a rebound in AI stocks, with Nvidia (NVDA), AMD (AMD), and Intel (INTC) posting notable gains.

Elsewhere, a better-than-expected jobs report is also driving the S&P 500 higher. Nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000, shattering expectations of 70,000. On top of that, August's payroll growth was revised up to 186,000 from 133,000, while September's was raised to 60,000 from 29,000.

In addition, the unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%, below the estimate of 4.2%. The rate has trended between 4.1% and 4.3% since March.

Should You Buy the S&P 500?

Wall Street is bullish on the S&P 500 ETF (SPY). During the past three months, analysts have issued an average SPY price target of $987.88, implying upside of 33.43% from current prices. The 503 holdings in SPY carry 414 buy ratings, 83 hold ratings, and six sell ratings, reflecting strong overall sentiment across the index. The highest price target is at $1,220.09, while the lowest sits at $765.16.
